introduction.p: In this activity, we consider sets of linear equations having just two unknowns. In this case, we can graph the solutions sets for the equations, which allows us to visualize different types of behavior.
Please complete your work on a sheet of paper. When you have finished, you can scan it and upload it at the end of this activity.

statement.p: At what point or points (x,y), do the lines intersect? How many points (x,y) satisfy both equations?

image.shortdescription: A coordinate grid and axes for plotting two lines.

description.p: A coordinate grid and axes where the horizontal and vertical coordinates range from -4 to 4. There are no other features as the reader is asked to graph two lines with this image as a guide.

sidebyside.p: The graph of the two lines is as shown on the right. There is a single point, the point (2,3), at which the lines intersect. Therefore, there is a single point that satisfies both equations.

answer.p: This is exactly one point, the point (2,3), that satisfies both equations.

statement.p: At what point or points (x,y), do the lines intersect? How many points (x,y) satisfy both equations?

image.shortdescription: A coordinate grid and axes for plotting two lines.

description.p: A coordinate grid and axes where the horizontal and vertical coordinates range from -4 to 4. There are no other features as the reader is asked to graph two lines with this image as a guide.

sidebyside.p: These two lines are parallel, which means there is no point at which the lines intersect. Therefore, there is no point that satisfies both equations.

answer.p: There are no points that satisfy both equations.

statement.p:
On the grid below, graph the line
y = x+1 .
How many points (x,y) satisfy this equation?

image.shortdescription: A coordinate grid and axes for plotting two lines.

description.p: A coordinate grid and axes where the horizontal and vertical coordinates range from -4 to 4. There are no other features as the reader is asked to graph two lines with this image as a guide.

sidebyside.p: There are infinitely many points that lie on this line and that, therefore, satisfy this single equation.

statement.p: At what point or points (x,y), do the lines intersect? How many points (x,y) satisfy all three equations?

image.shortdescription: A coordinate grid and axes for plotting two lines.

description.p: A coordinate grid and axes where the horizontal and vertical coordinates range from -4 to 4. There are no other features as the reader is asked to graph two lines with this image as a guide.

sidebyside.p: These three lines do not have a common intersection point. Consequently, there is no point satisfying all three equations.

answer.p: There are no points that satisfy all three equations.
